item.title: Valkyries ready for prime time but WNBA stuck in amateur hour with Game 6 debacle
item.description: Golden State Valkyries fans celebrate on Monday during Game 5 of the WNBA Finals against the Atlanta Dream at Chase Center. (Santiago Mejia/S.F. Chronicle) Throughout this crazy run, the Golden State Valkyries ' fans have been the team's secret weapon; their love affair creating a frenzied and overwhelming home-court advantage. That asset was on full display in Monday night's Game 5, in a physical 64-55 win over the Atlanta Dream before a deafening full house at Chase Center. Now, just one victory away from their first WNBA championship, what is the team's message to its devoted fans? "As much as we love Ballhalla, we don't want to come back here," center Kiah Stokes said. "We need to go in (to Thursday's game) with the mentality that we have to win." So get your coffee ready, pick up some bagels, (maybe some bubbly unless you're really superstitious) and embrace the absurdity of the situation the WNBA has created. The Valkyries will play their next game on Thursday in Atlanta beginning at 9:30 a.m. PDT and will be trying to wrap up a championship before lunch time. "Call in sick," guard Veronica Burton said. "I recommend it." Stokes coughed into the microphone. "Y'all know how to fake a cough, we can all do that," she said. "I'm sure they'll be supporting us at whatever time." Monday began with the WNBA making headlines for the wrong reasons. Still unsure of where and when Game 6 would be played in Atlanta, just three days before it was to be held, the league finally announced its solution late Monday morning. The teams would play a weekday matinee at State Farm Arena, allowing the NBA's Hawks, who control the arena, to play their scheduled evening game against Cleveland. It was a clumsy solution. But the alternatives would have been almost as bad, either disrupting the entire series schedule by adding several extra days, or playing in the evening in the tiny, 3,500-seat arena the Dream have called home most of the season. Or as Warriors coach Steve Kerr put it Monday, when asked about the situation before the his team's game, "It's better than having it at the YMCA in front of 75 people." Still, it creates horrible small-time optics in what should be the league's shining moment. It probably means sacrificing millions of television viewers and the revenue that comes with them, in order to sell 14,000 extra seats. And it adds a layer of perception that women playing in a championship have to take a back seat to men's teams playing an October regular-season game - one fan at Chase waved a sign that read "Move the Hawks Game, Women = Prime Time." Reports have indicated the NBA could have made accommodations with the Hawks' and their opponent's schedules if given enough time. The real fault was the complete lack of foresight by the Dream, and the WNBA, to make sure there were contingency plans in place for a team that was in the playoff hunt the entire season and steamrolling by late August. item.description: Mandatory Credit: Cary Edmondson-Imagn Images Steve Kerr has YMCA jokes for Valkyries ahead of early WNBA Finals Game 6 appeared first on ClutchPoints . Steve Kerr will be up bright and early to support the Golden State Valkyries on Thursday, and the Warriors coach is not complaining about the unusual tipoff time for Game 6 of the WNBA Finals . With the Valkyries holding a 3-2 series lead over the Atlanta Dream , Game 6 is set for 12:30 p.m. ET, or 9:30 a.m. in the Bay Area. When asked about the early start, Kerr joked that he would be watching over breakfast. “We’ll be having breakfast at about that time, I think,” Kerr said, via Joseph Dycus . “I guess we’ll have a day off that day, so yeah, I’ll be watching.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “It's better than, you know, having it at the YMCA that night in front of 75 people.” Warriors coach Steve Kerr on Valkyries-Dream game 6 in Atlanta being at 9:30am on Thursday. pic.twitter.com/tvnOxzPmA3 — Joseph Dycus (@joseph_dycus) October 27, 2026 Kerr then took a lighthearted jab at the alternative. “Better than, you know, having it at the YMCA that night, you know, in front of 75 people,” Kerr said. “So they’re doing what they’ve got to do.” The Warriors coach was poking fun at the scheduling saga that has surrounded the series. Game 6 was originally set for 8 p.m. ET at Gateway Center Arena, the Dream’s 3,500-seat home and the smallest venue in the WNBA. The league later moved the game to State Farm Arena, home of the Atlanta Hawks, which seats roughly 17,000. The catch is that the Hawks host the Cleveland Cavaliers at State Farm Arena that same night. The NBA pushed that game back an hour to 8 p.m. ET , but the arena still needed time to turn over, forcing the Finals game into an afternoon slot. The decision drew criticism, with many pointing out that a weekday lunchtime tip makes it tough for fans to tune in, especially on the West Coast. It is not the first change of the series, either, as Games 3 and 4 were also shifted to State Farm Arena. Kerr, however, is taking a glass-half-full approach. The Warriors and Valkyries share ownership and a home at Chase Center, and Kerr and several Warriors players have shown up to support the expansion franchise since its debut in 2025. The Valkyries put themselves one win away from their first championship with a 64-55 victory in Game 5 on Monday night at Chase Center. Kiah Stokes led the way with a season-high 13 points, eight rebounds and three blocks . A win on Thursday would give Golden State the title in just its second season, and Kerr will be watching over breakfast. item.title: Stephen Curry praises ‘complete package’ Yaxel Lendeborg after breakout NBA performance
item.description: Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images Yaxel Lendeborg’s huge performance against the Denver Nuggets has led to high praise from Golden State Warriors superstar Stephen Curry. Yaxel Lendeborg made headlines in his first NBA game ever by not backing down in a confrontation with Luka Doncic. The Warriors lost that game against the Lakers, and the next two as well. This streak ended on Monday night, and it was largely thanks to Lendeborg himself. The 24-year-old may have gotten his ‘welcome to the NBA’ moment when Doncic hit that shot from halfcourt, but against the Denver Nuggets, it was Yaxel who announced his arrival. The young star led the Warriors in scoring as they got their first win of the season against the Denver Nuggets. Stephen Curry describes how Yaxel Lendeborg’s ‘composure and feel’ make him a matchup problem When Lendeborg made his now infamous comments about Doncic, many of his detractors suggested he should play at a high level before he says all this. In the Warriors’ 134-114 win, Lendeborg put up 31 points, 12 rebounds, and six assists, a superstar performance by any metric. After the game, a visibly pleased Stephen Curry showered the rookie with praise, giving him some big compliments. “His composure. I mean, he just came off a NCAA Championship run and he’s just got composure and feel,” Curry said. “His size on the court, he’s a matchup problem. He’s not ever really in a hurry and he’s starting to see the picture really well. Distributing, being aggressive, getting to the free throw line, offensive rebounding. Kind of the full package. So we want him to continue playing aggressive.” If Lendeborg can establish himself as a productive starter as a rookie, that would be a massive boon to a struggling Warriors team. He has shown he has the ability to play at the highest level, and this is now something he simply has to produce with consistency. item.title: AC Milan plot SHOCK move for Bruno Fernandes after Man Utd relationship breakdown
item.description: FBL-ENG-PR-MAN UTD-BOURNEMOUTH - AFP AC Milan are closely monitoring Bruno Fernandes following a complete breakdown in his relationship with Manchester United ahead of the January window. The Portugal midfielder could push for an imminent departure after publicly criticising the club's ambition and subsequently losing his place in the starting line-up under Michael Carrick. Milan monitor unhappy United star Milan are keeping a close eye on Fernandes ahead of the January transfer window, as per Calciomercato . The Portugal midfielder is reportedly unhappy at United, and his relationship with the club has completely broken down. The same report suggest that Fernandes is actively pushing for a winter exit. Rossoneri manager Ruben Amorim is driving the interest, as he hopes to secure a reunion with his former captain. The situation at Old Trafford has deteriorated rapidly in recent weeks. Fernandes has grown frustrated with the current regime, sparking widespread speculation over his long-term future in England. Midfielder clashes with Carrick Tensions reached a boiling point after the Red Devils suffered a heavy 4-1 Champions League defeat to Como . Following the loss, Fernandes publicly criticised the club's overall mentality. The midfielder claimed that United focus far too much on their past glories instead of looking towards the future. These comments reportedly caused friction and led to immediate repercussions for the 32-year-old. Carrick publicly disagreed with his player's harsh assessment of the situation. Consequently, Fernandes was dropped to the bench for their weekend Premier League defeat against Bournemouth at Old Trafford. Amorim plans tactical Serie A return A move to Milan would mark a return to Serie A for Fernandes. The playmaker previously enjoyed spells in Italy with Udinese and Sampdoria. Amorim already knows Fernandes well from their shared time at Old Trafford. The Milan boss believes the Portuguese star would thrive in one of the two attacking roles behind the striker in his preferred 3-4-2-1 tactical system. However, significant financial hurdles remain for the Italian side. Fernandes currently earns €10.2 million net per season, which is well beyond what Milan can comfortably afford. Sacrifices needed for January deal Both the player and the club will need to make major financial sacrifices to make the transfer a reality. Fernandes rejected lucrative offers from Saudi Arabia in the summer, proving he still values top-level European football. His current United contract runs until June 2027, though talks over any extension have stalled entirely. United also hold an option to extend the deal by a further year, which they could trigger to protect his transfer value and avoid losing him for free. The Premier League side could still demand a substantial fee, as his contract includes a release clause of almost €65m for foreign clubs. Milan will need to negotiate fiercely if they want to secure their prime target this winter.

item.title: LeBron James Is NOT the GOAT, But His Fans Need to Hear This
item.description: Oct 22, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; General view as Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James stands for the anthem before a game against the Cleveland Cavaliers at Xfinity Mobile Arena. Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images TPX IMAGES OF THE DAY Let’s have the argument one more time. LeBron James has built one of the greatest résumés in basketball history. Four NBA championships, four Finals MVPs, an all-time scoring record and an extraordinary level of longevity. Nobody serious can deny his place among the greatest players ever. But the greatest of all time? That’s where the debate gets uncomfortable. Michael Jordan went 6-0 in the NBA Finals. Six championships, six Finals MVPs and a peak that became the standard for an entire generation of basketball fans. LeBron has the longevity argument. Jordan has the championship argument. Both dominated their eras, and both have cases that go beyond counting rings. But here’s where LeBron supporters sometimes lose the plot: being the most accomplished player and being the greatest player are not necessarily the same argument. And Jordan fans aren’t automatically wrong just because they prefer a different standard. LeBron’s career is legendary. That doesn’t mean the debate has to be over. If your GOAT needs a 30-minute explanation every time somebody questions the ranking, is he really the undisputed GOAT? LeBron or Jordan? Pick your side. 👇

item.title: Andoni Iraola saves Liverpool £100m thanks to genius decision
item.description: Andoni Iraola saves Liverpool £100m thanks to genius decision Andoni Iraola's time at Liverpool has been fairly mixed so far. While he may have only lost one game across all competitions, the Reds are still nowhere near where they need to be in terms of performance. Every now and then, the Anfield outfit have managed to prove their worth and actually put on a good display but, more often than not, one area of their team has let them down or just not met the standards expected of them. This has caused fans to demand that even more players are signed in the next couple of transfer windows to finally try and get the Reds back on track. But, one thing Iraola has done well is get the most out of Liverpool's youngsters and, after the recent performances of one, he may have saved the Anfield outfit around £100 million. Andoni Iraola's decision to keep Trey Nyoni may have saved Liverpool £100m The summer transfer window was fairly mad. Over £100 million pounds were spent on single players by many different clubs with Manchester City even adding two to their ranks. The fact that midfielders such as Elliot Anderson and Ayyoub Bouaddi were going for that much money was obscene . Inflation has massively rocked the transfer market but, since Iraola managed to keep Trey Nyoni at Anfield, he could have just saved them over £100 million. At the moment, Alex Scott seems to be the Reds' prime midfield target and, while he'd be a good signing, the £100 million that Bournemouth are demanding for him feels rather steep. That's why, the recent performances of Nyoni are rather exciting. And, it's clear that Iraola thinks the same way after what he said to El Boro in an interview on their YouTube Channel. "He’s surprised me. As soon as I arrived, I saw him and thought, ‘There’s a proper footballer here,'" he said . Trey Nyoni could be the next big thing to emerge from Liverpool Although Nyoni is only 19 years old now, he's already performing to an extremely high standard. The Englishman has featured in eight games this season and, although he's been used in a double pivot, something he hasn't ever done before, he's performed extremely well. Of course, since he's so young, he can't be expected to play two 90 minute games of football each week but, even if he can just play one, it would help Liverpool out massively. His development has been going extremely well over the last couple of months and, if he continues on this upward trajectory, there's no knowing how good he could eventually become. Obviously, reinforcement is still needed among the Reds' midfield but, for now, Nyoni looks likely to be an excellent option for Liverpool. item.title: 'I would do it again' - Kaepernick reflects on price of protest, 10 years on
item.description: [Getty Images] "I would absolutely do it again." Ten years on from making the gesture that catapulted him to iconic status, but which he believes led to his exile from the sport he loved, Colin Kaepernick insists he has no regrets. It was September 2016 when NFL star Kaepernick knelt during the US national anthem before a match as a peaceful protest against racial injustice and police brutality. It proved both inspirational and divisive. In his first interview with BBC Sport since then, Kaepernick reflects on his journey; his pride at seeing England footballers take the knee, athlete activism, the relationship between sport and politics, and the price he paid for being a figurehead for the civil rights movement. "I knew the protest could potentially cost me my career," he says. "History shows us…that is a reality for athletes. "We also see this in broader movements, going well beyond costing someone their career, and costing people their lives. We see Malcolm X assassinated, we see MLK [Martin Luther King] assassinated, so the consequences are real." Having initially sat to protest against the plight of black people in the US, Kaepernick first knelt during the Star-Spangled Banner before his San Francisco 49ers team played a pre-season game. It was an act he would repeat before 11 regular-season contests that year. At the time, he said he could not stand up for - and show pride in - a flag "for a country that oppresses black people and people of colour", adding: "This is bigger than football and it would be selfish on my part to look the other way." His stance against racial inequality was seen as heroic by many, inspiring other NFL players to follow suit. But there was also condemnation from those who said it was disrespectful to the military. Those dissenting voices included Donald Trump - then a presidential candidate. Trump described the act as "a terrible thing" and unpatriotic. He even suggested Kaepernick should find another country to live in, adding players who refused to stand for the national anthem should be fired. The NFL said it would fine teams whose players did not stand. Kaepernick opted out of his contract with the 49ers in March 2017, though the club's management later said he would have been released regardless. Despite leading the 49ers to the 2013 Super Bowl, and throwing 16 touchdowns in his final season, one of the most talented quarterbacks in the sport never found a new team. Speaking from New York, Kaepernick says he anticipated the reaction to taking the knee. "What I couldn't have predicted was the people who would show up for me in significant ways, and also the people who worked against me and against the movement," he adds. Kaepernick eventually filed a grievance against NFL team owners, who he believed had conspired not to hire him because of his protests, reaching a financial settlement in 2019. item.description: [BBC] English Ballon d'Or winners have been few and far between. Triumphs to be treasured, names never to be forgotten. Harry Kane, England's great talisman and captain, is the first to claim football's grandest individual accolade in 25 years after a sensational campaign in Bayern Munich colours - and only the fifth Englishman to ever do so. Before him Michael Owen, in 2001, was the first Three Lions star to take it since Kevin Keegan's successive triumphs 22 years earlier. England World Cup winner Bobby Charlton did it in 1966, and that came after Stanley Matthews won the inaugural prize a decade earlier - handed what began life as the European Footballer of the Year award in 1956. Others have come close - Billy Wright, Bobby Moore, Gary Lineker, David Beckham and Frank Lampard are all among the runners-up. Lucy Bronze, in 2019, and Beth Mead, 2022, also more recently finished second. Of course, the award has gradually evolved into the global behemoth it is today. The caveat with those earlier winners is that it was not a worldwide prize - until 1995 it was only open to European players, and only in 2007 did it expand to include all players from all clubs across the world. However, that does not detract from the award-winning performances these stars produced - each enjoyed prize-worthy campaigns that caught voters' eyes across Europe and the world. But who among the five to have held the coveted prize is England's greatest Ballon d'Or winner? 5. Michael Owen, Liverpool, 2001 Only Brazil's Ronaldo, in 1997, was younger than Owen when he won the Ballon d'Or in 2001 [Getty Images] We won't hold it against Michael Owen for suggesting he didn't know what the Ballon d'Or was when Gerard Houllier first rang to announce he'd won it. And, in fairness, the then 22-year-old swotted up sufficiently by the time he received the award, reeling off a list of previous winners. Owen in those days, even after his initial hamstring struggles, was explosive, electric - searing pace and acceleration complemented by the most ruthless of finishes. He became a renowned goalscorer in his teenage years and, by 2001, was one of the most sought-after youngsters in world football. Owen's Ballon d'Or-winning year was one of iconic moments. He helped Liverpool to a treble, clinching the League Cup on penalties before beating Arsenal in the FA Cup final - Owen scored twice late on to turn the game in Liverpool's favour. The leveller was an acrobatic and clinically taken strike inside the Arsenal box, the winner a devastating break in which the prolific striker darted away from Lee Dixon and Tony Adams before slotting past David Seaman with his left foot. More importantly, his production has appeared in every victory, including the two games decided by one run. William Contreras’ defense strengthens Brewers’ World Series MVP case His defense makes that offensive consistency even more valuable. In the 3-2 Game 1 win, Contreras threw out Victor Mesa Jr. at third and Jonathan Aranda at second to end consecutive innings. Those were immediate, measurable contributions to protecting a narrow lead. The Rays arrived with a running game capable of manufacturing offense. item.title: Amir Khan backs £500k fighter welfare campaign
item.description: Former world champion Amir Khan is backing a campaign to raise £500,000 for an investigation into fighter safety and welfare [Getty Images] Former boxing world champion Amir Khan and Liverpool's Paul Smith are backing a campaign to raise £500,000 to help investigate safety and welfare across combat sports. The Liverpool-based Global Fighters' Association (GFA) says the investigation will examine fighters' medical care, pay, contracts and support after retirement. The group campaigns for better working conditions for boxers and other combat sports says the inquiry, to be led by barrister Jonathan Caplan KC, will gather evidence from fighters, doctors, referees and promoters. Smith, a former British champion, told BBC News many fighters struggled with high medical costs and low earnings, and needed better protection. Paul Smith last fought in 2017 and says fighters need better protection and support [GFA] He said he had sometimes paid between £700 and £1,000 a year for medical tests during his career. Smith said some boxers competing at lower levels could earn only a few hundred pounds after expenses, despite spending weeks preparing for a fight. "We want to try and create some form of safety blanket for fighters," he said. Smith also spoke about the difficulties of adjusting to life after boxing. "You lose that purpose, you lose that identity, you lose your day-to-day routine," he said. Amir Khan (left), pictured fighting Kell Brook in 2022, is backing a campaign to improve safety and welfare in combat sports [Reuters] Khan, a co-founder of the GFA, said there needed to be an organisation fighters could turn to "when something goes wrong", whether during training, over contracts or after retirement. The fundraising campaign will support the investigation and the GFA's wider plans to establish a trade union. The British Boxing Board of Control, which regulates professional boxing in Britain, already requires annual medical examinations and brain scans. Its general secretary, Robert Smith, told BBC Sport earlier this year that the board provided insurance for death and permanent injury. item.title: NASCAR’s Old-School Fans Might Hate This Take
item.description: Photo by: Bob Goshert DALE EARNHARDT WOULD NOT AUTOMATICALLY DOMINATE TODAY’S NASCAR. THERE, WE SAID IT. Before anybody starts typing, take a breath. Dale Earnhardt was an icon. Richard Petty helped build the sport. Jeff Gordon changed its trajectory. Jimmie Johnson put together one of the most incredible championship runs in modern sports. Their legacies are secure. But NASCAR fans have a habit of acting like every driver from the past would automatically destroy today’s field — and that every current driver is somehow less talented because the sport has changed. Why? Today’s drivers compete with different cars, different technology, different aerodynamic packages and a level of data analysis that earlier generations could barely imagine. The competition evolves. The equipment evolves. The preparation evolves. And the drivers have to evolve with it. Kyle Larson has demonstrated extraordinary car control across multiple disciplines. Ryan Blaney, Christopher Bell, Chase Elliott and the rest of today’s top competitors are racing against elite opponents who have spent their lives mastering this sport. That doesn’t mean Larson is better than Earnhardt. Comparing drivers across eras is nearly impossible because the circumstances are so different. But it also doesn’t mean today’s stars deserve less respect. You cannot take a driver from 1985, drop him into a modern Cup car without preparation and declare the debate settled. Just as you cannot take a modern driver back several decades and assume the transition would be easy. Greatness is about what a driver accomplishes against the competition of his era. And if Larson continues stacking championships and victories, he deserves to be discussed alongside the legends — whether traditionalists like it or not. HERE’S THE QUESTION THAT WILL SPLIT NASCAR FANS DOWN THE MIDDLE: 🔥 Kyle Larson has the talent to be considered among the greatest drivers ever. 👎 No modern driver belongs in the same conversation as Earnhardt, Petty or Johnson until the résumé matches theirs. Pick your side. And if you’re choosing a legend over Larson, tell us exactly what separates them — championships, wins, versatility or something else entirely?

item.title: Javonte Williams' patience pays off with career-best performance in Cowboys' win vs. Eagles
item.description: Dallas Cowboys running back Javonte Williams (33) runs the ball ahead of Philadelphia Eagles linebacker Zack Baun (53) during the second half of an NFL football game at Lincoln Financial Field on Monday, Oct. 26, 2026, in Philadelphia. (Elías Valverde II/The Dallas Morning News) PHILADELPHIA — The Cowboys made it an emphasis to run the ball this week after mostly abandoning it through the first six weeks of the season. Starting running back Javonte Williams quickly showed the change was warranted. Williams ran for a career-high 155 yards and a touchdown on 25 carries. He said after the game that 25 carries was the goal the offensive coaches had for him in the team’s 38-21 win over the Eagles on Monday . Williams looked like he ran for a career-high after the game. His No. 33 jersey was not only covered in grass stains from Lincoln Financial Field, but it also had a significant blood spot. “It was good. I mean, just to give the confidence to keep calling the runs,” Williams said after the game. The offensive line played a big part of that, too. Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott even wore a shirt that said “linemen lead the way” to his postgame news conference. “The holes were wide open,” Williams said, “and I was just running through it.” Williams showed patience to let those holes open. He also showed patience through the first six games of the season. Williams didn’t have a game with more than 20 carries in that span. He had more than 12 carries in a game only twice. “He’s a true pro,” Prescott said of Williams. “One of the best teammates. The guy does everything right. Smart football player, physical football player. He’s a guy you have to get in the groove and that was probably one of the most frustrating things for him the last couple of weeks — is not getting the chance to get in a groove. “Tonight he had that chance.” The lack of carries was somewhat surprising, considering head coach Brian Schottenheimer’s offense is built on a balanced marriage between the run and the pass. They showed it last year when Williams ran for a career-high 1,201 rushing yards. It landed him a three-year extension this offseason . Game situations dictated the Cowboys' lack of running the ball at times during the first six weeks, but there were moments where they could’ve pursued it more. On Monday, they ensured they wouldn’t deviate from it . It worked. “It was coming,” Williams said about an eventual big game. “We’ve got a high level, high-powered offense. And I mean, when you’ve got [George Pickens], [CeeDee Lamb], Jake Ferguson, those guys on the outside, it’s going to open up the run lane.” Just like it did Monday. item.title: Manchester City owner Sheikh Mansour pumps extra £100m into club despite Premier League guilty verdict
item.description: Sheikh Mansour Manchester City - Getty Images Sheikh Mansour has reaffirmed his unwavering commitment to Manchester City by injecting a fresh £100 million into the club's parent company. The significant financial boost arrives at a turbulent moment for the Etihad outfit following a landmark ruling regarding their financial conduct. Fresh investment amid legal turmoil As reported by The Mirror , Sheikh Mansour has funnelled another £100m into the City Football Group (CFG) during a tumultuous period for the eight-time Premier League champions. Recent Companies House filings revealed the creation of over 11.3 million new shares to generate the capital. Mansour's Newton Investment and Development firm snapped up the entire allocation, slightly bolstering his majority stake in CFG. The parent company, which boasts a sprawling portfolio of global clubs including Girona, New York City, and Palermo, currently commands a valuation approaching £6 billion. Unwavering support behind the scenes Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan Manchester City The financial injection serves as a clear statement of intent from the Abu Dhabi ownership, arriving just weeks after an independent commission found City guilty of 114 out of 115 Premier League financial charges . Despite this severe legal setback, Mansour is evidently doubling down on his commitment to the global footballing empire. City have vehemently maintained their innocence throughout the sprawling, multi-year investigation. The club quickly confirmed their intention to lodge a formal appeal , ensuring that the unprecedented legal war with the English top flight will continue in front of a new, separate independent panel. Soriano mounts a staunch defence While Mansour has refrained from speaking publicly about the charges, City CEO Ferran Soriano addressed the situation head-on in a lengthy internal message to staff. He heavily criticised the commission's ruling, arguing it ignored extensive evidence provided by the club that proved owner funds were never disguised as independent sponsorships. Soriano stated: "This has gone for so long that it is important to remind ourselves that the whole Premier League case against us is based on a single false accusation - that the owners' personal money was somehow and secretly put into the club via some sponsors from Abu Dhabi. This is just not true." He added that the commission's conclusion was "clearly wrong" and leaned on a Premier League "conspiracy theory". Drawing parallels to the club's successful 2020 appeal against UEFA at the Court of Arbitration for Sport, Soriano vowed that City would be relentless in pursuing all legal avenues to clear their name, protect the institution, and potentially seek compensation.
